title: Surgical Apgar Score
sources: Gawande AA et al. J Am Coll Surg 2007; Regenbogen SE et al. (validation) Ann Surg 2009
purpose: A 10-point score calculated from three intraoperative parameters at the end of general / abdominal surgery, predicting 30-day major complications and death. Uses data the anaesthetic record already contains.

options.label: > 85 (or any pathologic bradyarrhythmia incl. asystole / VF requiring CPR)

interpretation.label: High risk — 30-day major complication / death rate ~ 55% at 0–2 and ~ 16% at 3–4. Strongly consider ICU / step-down admission, closer nursing, and a lower threshold for early re-evaluation
Intermediate risk — complication rate ~ 8%. Ward with enhanced vigilance; use clinical context and procedure to decide monitored bed
Low risk — complication rate ~ 4%. Routine postoperative care
Very low risk — complication rate ~ 4% or less; consider suitability for early discharge pathways

notes: The lowest HR item can exceed 3 points (≤ 55 = 4), so the maximum is 10. Score at the end of the operation. It reflects intraoperative course, not baseline risk — combine with a preoperative index (RCRI, NSQIP, ASA class) for the full picture. A low score should change disposition and handoff, not just documentation.
